page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the ratio
steps.margin_note: First mark. A coordinate plane is where one coordinate is ZERO, so the XZ-plane divides the join in the ratio −y₁ : y₂ — the two y-coordinates, with a minus on the first.

The ratio in which the XZ plane divides AB is

recall.must_convey: That the XZ-plane divides AB in the ratio −y₁ : y₂.
accept: the ratio is minus the first coordinate to the second
the plane is where that coordinate is zero so use minus y one to y two
write the ratio from the two y coordinates
ratio minus y one ratio y two

steps.why: The XZ-plane is exactly the set of points whose y-coordinate is zero, so asking where it cuts AB is asking where y becomes zero along AB — and the section formula turns that into this ratio directly.
common_mistakes: Using the wrong coordinate for the plane named.
Dropping the minus sign, which reverses internal and external division.

steps.label: Find the point of intersection
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Put that ratio into the section formula. A NEGATIVE ratio means the plane cuts the line EXTERNALLY, outside the segment — a real answer, not an error.

m x two plus n x one over m plus n for each coordinate

heard_as: m x two plus n x one

steps.why: A negative ratio is the standard signal for EXTERNAL division, and it is what makes the denominator m + n small — which is why the coordinates can come out large.
common_mistakes: Swapping m and n in the section formula.
Treating a negative ratio as an error and flipping its sign.
